38 Which list contains only fundamental particles?
A
antineutrinos, baryons, neutrons, electrons
B
mesons, electrons, neutrinos, protons
C
positrons, quarks, hadrons, protons
D
quarks, positrons, neutrinos, leptons

hints: Look at the words baryons, neutrons, mesons, hadrons and protons in the lists - decide which of these are composite particles made from quarks.
Recall that fundamental means with no internal structure, and in this syllabus the two fundamental families are quarks and leptons.
Test each list word by word: electrons, positrons, neutrinos and antineutrinos are all leptons, so reject any list that also contains even one hadron.
walkthrough: Identify what fundamental means: a particle with no internal structure that is not made of smaller particles.
Recall the syllabus groups: quarks are fundamental, and leptons such as electrons, positrons, neutrinos and antineutrinos are fundamental.
Recall the composite group: hadrons, which include baryons such as protons and neutrons, and mesons, are all made of quarks.
Check lists A, B and C: each contains at least one hadron - baryons and neutrons in A, mesons and protons in B, hadrons and protons in C - so each fails the only test.
Check the remaining list: quarks are fundamental, and positrons, neutrinos and leptons are all leptons and therefore fundamental, so every member is fundamental. This is option D.

A.explanation: Antineutrinos and electrons are fundamental leptons, but baryons and neutrons are hadrons made of three quarks so are not fundamental.

B.explanation: Electrons and neutrinos are fundamental leptons, but mesons and protons are hadrons made of quarks so are not fundamental.

C.explanation: Positrons and quarks are fundamental, but hadrons and protons are composite particles made of quarks so are not fundamental.

D.explanation: Quarks are fundamental, and positrons, neutrinos and leptons are all members of the lepton family which has no internal structure.
